version.changelog: v2.3 quality enhancement - security audit + marketing packaging + slug-content validation

llm.summary: This RSS-to-Markdown skill has a coherent purpose, but its examples use unrestricted URL fetching and under-scoped local file writes that users should review carefully.

dimensions.detail: Network access and exec-driven scripting are expected for fetching RSS feeds, but the examples do not restrict URL schemes, private/internal hosts, redirects, response size, or content type.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package appears to be Markdown instructions and examples, with no bundled executable installer; it does instruct users to install the common requests dependency and run generated scripts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Activation text includes broad non-RSS triggers such as document generation, design, and machine learning, which is wider than the stated RSS-to-Markdown purpose.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Saving files is purpose-aligned, but output paths and explicit filenames are not consistently constrained, and examples derive filenames from untrusted feed item titles while opening files in overwrite mode.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The RSS conversion purpose is coherent, but the documented implementation accepts arbitrary feed URLs with raw requests.get and writes generated Markdown/JSON locally, creating SSRF and overwrite risks without enough containment.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing or using this skill in an agent with access to private networks or important local files. Only use trusted public RSS/Atom URLs, keep output inside a dedicated directory, avoid title-derived filenames, and require confirmation before overwriting files or running generated scripts.
llm.findings:
[T09] expected: RSS fetching is expected, but the artifact-backed requests.get examples fetch user-supplied URLs without validation, so the SSRF concern is material rather than merely theoretical.
[T09] expected: Local Markdown export is expected, but the save examples allow caller-supplied filenames and title-derived filenames without path containment or overwrite protection.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad trigger wording is not aligned with a narrow RSS/feed conversion skill and could cause unexpected activation for unrelated document or machine-learning requests.
[SQP-2] expected: Saving Markdown and feed metadata is core functionality, but the artifact does not clearly warn about output location, overwrite behavior, or persisting untrusted remote feed content.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The batch-conversion examples conflict with the stated free-edition single-source limit; this is an inconsistency and under-disclosure issue, not evidence of malicious behavior.
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese-only documentation matches the Chinese display name and apparent audience, so this was downgraded as a security concern.
[SDI-4] expected: The 'safe get element text' wording overstates a small helper's guarantees, but it is a minor documentation precision issue compared with the URL and file-write risks.
